The day's crypto news is a mixture of market positioning, fund flows, policy updates, and company decisions. The headlines below are worth reading for the detail behind them, not just the reaction on a price chart.

What is moving the conversation

Securitize pushes into $6 trillion asset-backed finance market with River One acquisition. The tokenization firm unveiled an acquisition and a $50 million stock buyback as quarterly revenue rose 13%. SECZ shares jumped 10% after hours. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Robinhood backs tokenization of its stock on OKX–ICE platform even as most companies opt out. The brokerage firm said it would rather help build tokenized markets than sit on the sidelines, following a wave of early corporate pushback to the Intercontinental Exchange and OKX joint venture. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

A Bitcoin block just neared a 2015 transaction record, but paid only $180 in fees. The AntPool block came within 984 transactions of Bitcoin’s 2015 record, even as fees made up less than 0.1% of the miner’s payout. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Google’s AI chip push adds more pressure on Nvidia. Google’s specialised AI chips threaten greater competition as Nvidia faces a leadership investigation. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

North Korean hackers are creating memecoins to wash loot from $6.3 billion Binance hack. North Korean hackers used six homemade memecoins to launder 117,000 NEAR, worth about $430,000, from the $6.3 billion Binance hack, Elliptic says. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

NYSE picks Avalanche to settle tokenized stocks amid Wall Street's blockchain race. Avalanche will serve as the core settlement ledger for the exchange's planned blockchain stock market Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Market context

Bitcoin is around $75,106 with a +0.52% 24-hour move, while Ether is around $2,130.59 with a -0.36% move. Those figures are a snapshot, not a forecast. The useful question is whether the move is supported by spot demand, volume, and a clear change in the news.

When the market is quiet, leverage and liquidity can matter as much as direction. A small headline can move price quickly when traders are positioned too closely on one side.

What to watch next

  • New ETF creations and redemptions.
  • Futures open interest and funding rates.
  • Fresh regulatory text or official statements.
  • Security warnings, outages, or custody changes.
  • Whether the reported developments become live products rather than announcements.

The fairest reading today is cautious attention. There are real developments in the industry, but none should be stretched into a guaranteed market direction.

items.title: Crypto ETFs End 8-Week Outflow Streak With $282M Inflows as Bitcoin and Ethereum Demand Rebounds
items.description:
After two months of relentless selling pressure, cryptocurrency exchange-traded funds (ETFs) have finally posted their first week of positive flows, signaling a potential improvement in institutional sentiment toward digital assets.

Global crypto investment products attracted $281.8 million in net inflows last week, ending an eight-week stretch of outflows that erased more than $7 billion from the sector. [...] Daily flows reflected continued uncertainty among investors. Funds attracted more than $265 million on July 6, the strongest single-day inflow since early May, before sharply slowing the following day.

The middle of the week saw renewed outflows before demand recovered again on Friday with another positive session.

Despite the improvement, the latest inflows remain small compared with the more than $8 billion that exited Bitcoin ETFs over the previous eight weeks. [...] US-listed spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $197.4 million in net inflows during the week ending July 10, breaking an eight-week streak of outflows that had persisted since the second week of May.

The weekly figure was driven primarily by BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT), which continued to dominate the market.

IBIT attracted nearly $292 million during the week, offsetting significant withdrawals from Grayscale's GBTC, Fidelity's FBTC, and ARK 21Shares' Bitcoin ETF.

items.title: 2025 Crypto Regulatory Round-Up
items.description:
What is the GENIUS Act and how does it regulate stablecoins?

The GENIUS Act is United States legislation passed in 2025 that establishes a federal regulatory framework for stablecoin issuers. It mandates strict requirements for reserve backing, audits, and financial integrity. The law also places restrictions on the domestic offering of foreign issued stablecoins, prompting a global acceleration in stablecoin policy development. [...] National regulators that have not yet developed or implemented stablecoin regulation will continue to make progress. By July 2026, U.S. federal and state regulators are required to promulgate final regulations to implement the GENIUS Act. This will include processes to license and regulate federal stablecoin issuers, and establishing criteria that foreign stablecoin issuers must meet in order to offer their stablecoins in the U.S. In Singapore, draft legislation to implement a stablecoin regime [...] Throughout the region, regulators are paying much closer attention to the systemic role of stablecoins — particularly their use in cross‑border payments, trade settlement, and inflation hedging — and are starting to define clearer requirements around issuance, reserve backing, redemption rights, and intermediary obligations, with FATF alignment and upcoming mutual evaluations serving as a common anchor for AML/CFT expectations and supervisory priorities.

Notably, the GENIUS Act prohibits issuers from paying holders any form of interest or yield (cash, tokens or other consideration) for holding and use of payment stablecoin. Issuers are considered financial institutions subject to the Bank Secrecy Act (the “BSA”) with responsibilities to comply with US sanctions, anti-money laundering, customer identification, due diligence and other related laws. Holders of payment stablecoins will have a priority claim to segregated reserve assets that is [...] In a flurry of pre-recess activity, Congress recently made headway on two pieces of legislation with significant impacts for the digital asset industry, the Guiding and Establishing National Innovation for US Stablecoins Act (the “GENIUS Act”), which passed both chambers of Congress and was signed into law by the President on July 18, 2025, and the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act of 2025 (the “CLARITY Act”), which has thus far only passed the House but builds upon components of earlier [...] Federal government agencies will be engaging in notice and comment rulemaking or issuing guidance to carry out the various implementation needs that the GENIUS Act and a potential market framework law, such as CLARITY, present. These rulemakings will presumably be exempt from the administration’s strict controls on new rulemakings.
 Those wishing to apply to issue stablecoins can begin submitting applications as of approximately July 2026.

items.title: Cryptocurrency Regulation: A Guide to U.S. & Global Policies | Britannica Money
items.description:
Cryptocurrency regulation is no longer a theoretical debate—it’s an evolving framework that is beginning to take shape worldwide. In the United States, Congress has moved toward establishing federal oversight of stablecoins and digital asset markets. The GENIUS Act, signed into law in 2025, established a federal regulatory framework for stablecoins, while broader market structure legislation known as the CLARITY Act advanced in Congress in 2026 but has yet to become law. [...] United Kingdom. The U.K. began regulating cryptocurrency in 2020. In October 2023, the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) introduced stricter rules on crypto advertising. The Financial Services and Markets Act 2023 also expanded oversight of stablecoins. A broader regulatory framework was approved in 2026 and is scheduled to take effect in October 2027, bringing activities including crypto trading, custody, staking, and stablecoin issuance under FCA oversight. [...] ## Key Points

 U.S. cryptocurrency regulation is evolving: Federal law now governs stablecoins, while broader legislation defining oversight of digital asset markets remains unresolved.
 Governments globally have adopted widely varying approaches to digital asset regulation, from permissive frameworks to outright bans.
 U.S. oversight is divided among regulators, including the SEC and CFTC, with the IRS treating cryptocurrency as property for federal tax purposes.
